properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following river in Illinois...
Indiana...

Wabash River at Hutsonville to Vincennes

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crested. Flooding should come to an end
on the Wabash over the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Considerable agricultural flooding extends
from just north of the junction of Illinois 33 with Business 50 to
the St. Francesville, Illinois area.  River Road from Lincoln
Memorial Bridge to Billett Rd is impassable.  Extensive seep water
forms behind Illinois levees extending from Russellville to U.S.
Highway 50.  Flooding of agricultural land begins in Knox County
Indiana west of the railroad extending for the Oaktown area to the
north side of Vincennes.  Extensive flooding of Small Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 PM CDT /5:45 PM EDT/ Saturday the stage was 16.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 PM CDT /5:45 PM EDT/ Saturday was 17.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 4.4 feet Tuesday, September
08.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 915 AM CDT /1015
AM EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 29 at 5:52PM MDT until August 29 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Eastern Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 845 PM MDT.

* At 552 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across Dry Rock Creek and lower portions of Hole in the
Rock Road down to Lake Powell, including Headless Hen Canyon,
Coyote Gulch, Forty Mile Gulch, Fifty Mile Gulch, and Davis Gulch.
Up to 0.75 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Dry Rock Creek and lower portions of Hole in the Rock Road down to
Lake Powell, including Headless Hen Canyon, Coyote Gulch, Forty
Mile Gulch, Fifty Mile Gulch, and Davis Gulch.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 29 at 7:40PM CDT until August 29 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
At 740 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles southeast of
Seneca, or 15 miles west of Faulkton, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Two inch hail and 70 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
considerable tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to
mobile homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Seneca around 745 PM CDT.
Burkmere around 750 PM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. This storm is capable of producing
widespread damaging winds and dangerous hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 29 at 5:20PM MST until August 29 at 6:15PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
SVRTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
South Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 615 PM MST.

* At 520 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 11 miles east of
Topawa, moving northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Kitt Peak, South Komelik, Coldfields and Fresnal Canyon.

This includes Route 286 between mile markers 20 and 25.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.
